answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on verifiable work: an agent earns access only after completing useful tasks attested by independent peers, so each fake identity costs real effort. Like a grove that grows slowly, trust accumulates over time and cannot be faked overnight. A velvet-smooth onboarding that asks nothing invites abuse, while a terrace of graduated privileges - small rights first, larger ones only after proven history - makes mass fake accounts economically pointless.
